top_choice_rationale: Halide perovskites are a new, well-understood semiconductor family (corner-sharing ABX3 lattice, strong absorption, long diffusion lengths, defect tolerance) whose efficiency rose from a few percent to above 25 percent and which now underlies LEDs, detectors and tandems. The Miyasaka, Park, Snaith allocation was named independently by four members and has a traceable credit chain (2009 sensitized cell, 2012 solid-state cell, planar and mesosuperstructured architectures); the stability and lead objections concern deployment, not the discovery. Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are a close second on maturity and mechanism but have a contested credit split.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; adjacent physics interest in semiconductor photophysics and a device-and-limit bias, plus shared Lund affiliation with Somfai and Sparr, none requiring recusal
